about: Rocco's onboarding survey (docs/workflow/SETUP.md). Every answer is free text and optional. 'for' names the doc sections an answer feeds; ids are unique across flows and tiles, and a question shared by both flows keeps one id.

new.title: A new game
new.blurb: A few questions about the game and the first thing to build: enough for the pitch, the core of the design and the look, and a plan for the prototype that you approve before anything is built. Answer as much or as little as you like.

questions.hint: Describe it like you would to a friend. One sentence is plenty; more is welcome.
questions.placeholder: A pet-collecting game on floating islands, where...

questions.prompt: What does a player do, over and over?
questions.hint: The few steps they repeat, like explore, collect, upgrade, unlock the next area.

questions.prompt: What happens in a player's first few minutes?
questions.hint: From joining to the first reward, or the moment it clicks.
Rough ages, the kind of Roblox player, and whether they're mostly on phones or PCs.

questions.prompt: Which games is it like, and what's different about yours?
questions.hint: On Roblox or anywhere else.

questions.prompt: Why would someone come back tomorrow?
questions.hint: Progress, collecting, friends, events, daily rewards...

questions.prompt: What's the first thing you want to play?
questions.hint: The smallest version worth playtesting: the one moment that has to feel right, like drifting round a corner or catching your first pet. Everything else can wait.

questions.prompt: How does the player control it?
questions.hint: Keys, mouse, touch or a controller, and what each one does. Phone or PC first?
A flat test area is fine. Or a track, an island, a room: roughly how big, and what's in it.

questions.prompt: What should the first build leave out?
questions.hint: Menus, saving, shops, other players... anything that can wait until the core feels right.

questions.prompt: How will you know it's working?
questions.hint: What you'll look for the first time you play it.
A few words is enough: cozy, chunky, low-poly, bright, spooky...

questions.prompt: Any games, art or styles to look at?
questions.hint: Names or links. Images can come later.

questions.prompt: Anything you don't want in this game?
questions.hint: Ideas you've ruled out, or things you dislike in games like it.

questions.prompt: Anything else your agent should know?
questions.hint: A deadline, how you like to work, a name you're unsure of...

existing.title: A game I've already made
existing.blurb: Questions about how the game is built and where it stands. Then your agent brings it into the workflow, reads all of its code, and fills in the docs from what it finds.

questions.hint: Rojo, Argon, Lync, straight in Studio, packages from Wally... and where the code lives.
Not published, a private test, or public, and since when, roughly.
The game's link, or its experience and place ids, and whether it's on your account or a group.
Players, revenue, the numbers you watch. Rough is fine.
Describe it like you would to a friend.

questions.prompt: What do players do, over and over?
questions.hint: The few steps they repeat.
Rough ages, the kind of Roblox player, phones or PCs.
Game passes, developer products, subscriptions, with prices if you know them.
Just you, or others in Studio or on GitHub? Any place your agent must never touch, like a Team Create place?

questions.prompt: What do you want to work on next?
What's broken or messy right now?
Anything that must stay exactly as it is?
questions.hint: Systems, names, or data formats that players' saves depend on...

tiles.title: Monetization
tiles.blurb: What players can buy, and where the line is.

questions.hint: Game passes, items, currency, a season pass...
What must stay earnable by playing.
Or what matters more than money right now.

tiles.title: Economy
tiles.blurb: Currencies, where they come from and where they go.

questions.prompt: What do players earn and spend?
questions.hint: Coins, gems, materials: where each comes from and where it goes.

tiles.title: Progression
tiles.blurb: How a player grows over days and weeks.

questions.prompt: How does a player get stronger or further?
questions.hint: Levels, upgrades, unlocks, rebirths...
What keeps someone playing after a week.

tiles.title: World and map
tiles.blurb: Where it takes place, and how players get around.

questions.hint: The setting, and its areas.
Walking, teleports, areas that unlock, vehicles...

tiles.title: Characters and creatures
tiles.blurb: Who or what lives in the world.

questions.prompt: Who or what is in the world?
questions.hint: NPCs, creatures, pets, enemies, and how they look.

tiles.title: Content
tiles.blurb: What there is to find, collect or beat.

questions.prompt: What is there to find, collect or beat?
questions.hint: Items, areas, creatures, quests, and roughly how many at launch.

tiles.title: Social
tiles.blurb: Playing with and around other players.

questions.hint: Co-op, trading, competing, showing off, chat...
The style of music, the mood of the effects, games whose sound you like.

tiles.title: UI and devices
tiles.blurb: Screens, and the devices that matter most.

questions.hint: Phone, PC, tablet, console.
Minimal or busy, playful or clean, games whose menus you like.

tiles.title: Ideas for later
tiles.blurb: Things that aren't for the first version.

questions.prompt: Ideas for after the first version?

tiles.title: Risks and numbers
tiles.blurb: What could go wrong, and how you'll know it works.

questions.prompt: What worries you about this game?
How will you know it's working?
questions.hint: Players coming back the next day, time played, purchases...
